hypotheses.justification: hn follows from the other hypotheses. If n = 0, then hqn : ¬ (q:ℕ) ∣ 0 is false, because every number divides 0. So hqn alone gives n ≠ 0, and hence 0 < n. (hα also rules out n = 0: it would say 1 = (q:ℕ) in the algebraic closure, but q is prime.) The statement stays true after deleting hn. The proof only needs to start with `have hn : 0 < n := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (fun h => hqn (h ▸ dvd_zero _))`. The rest of the proof is unchanged, since it uses hn only through this local fact (for example in `Nat.mul_pos hn hd`, `hn.ne'`, and `zero_pow hn.ne'`).
